identity.title: MDAgents: An Adaptive Collaboration of LLMs for Medical Decision-Making

problem.claim: How to leverage LLMs effectively for complex medical decision-making tasks.

gap.claim: The best approach for using LLMs in complex medical tasks remains unresolved.

contributions.claim: MDAgents, a multi-agent framework that automatically assigns solo or group collaboration structures to LLM teams.
Evaluation across real-world medical knowledge and clinical diagnosis benchmarks, including comparison of medical-complexity classification with human physicians.
The framework uses medical-complexity assessment to adapt collaboration for efficiency and accuracy.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish MDAgents by automatically tailoring LLM collaboration structure to the medical task, inspired by task-adaptive real-world medical decision-making.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MDAgents achieved the best performance on seven of ten benchmarks, with improvements of up to 4.2% (p < 0.05) over previous methods’ best performances.
The authors report that moderator review combined with external medical knowledge in group collaboration improved average accuracy by 11.8%.
Ablation studies reportedly indicate that medical-complexity determination supports efficiency and accuracy across diverse medical tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are promising in medicine, but their use in complex medical tasks remains an open question.
MDAgents automatically assigns solo or group collaboration structures tailored to task complexity.
The framework and baselines are evaluated with state-of-the-art LLMs on medical knowledge and clinical diagnosis benchmarks, with physician comparison for complexity classification.
The authors report leading results on seven of ten benchmarks, up to 4.2% improvement, and an 11.8% average accuracy gain from moderator review plus external knowledge.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly connects collaboration structure to medical-task complexity and reports ablation evidence for this adaptive choice.

lessons.interpretation: A claim about multi-agent performance can be made more informative by exposing the routing or task-characterization mechanism behind it.
lessons.application: When presenting a collaborative system, specify which task property determines the collaboration mode and include an ablation isolating that adaptive decision.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when tasks are homogeneous or when routing overhead cannot be measured.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the ten benchmarks, datasets, models, or exact baseline configurations.
The reported gains do not specify confidence intervals, per-benchmark results, or the conditions under which external knowledge and moderator review were applied.
